subject: biology
title: Photosynthesis
key_idea: Plants and algae make their own food by photosynthesis. Carbon dioxide and water react to make glucose and oxygen. The reaction is endothermic: it takes in light energy, absorbed by chlorophyll in the chloroplasts.

blocks.text: Photosynthesis is a chemical reaction. This section covers what goes in, what comes out and how to write it.

items.meaning: The reaction in plants and algae that makes glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water, using light energy.
The green substance that absorbs light for photosynthesis.
The part of a plant or algal cell that contains chlorophyll, where photosynthesis happens.

blocks.label: Word equation for photosynthesis
where: carbon dioxide and water are the reactants
glucose and oxygen are the products
light energy is needed, and chlorophyll absorbs it (both are written above the arrow)

blocks.label: Symbol equation for photosynthesis
where: the reaction is endothermic, with light and chlorophyll above the arrow

items: Carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen.

Know the symbols CO₂, H₂O, C₆H₁₂O₆ and O₂.

sections.heading: An endothermic reaction in the chloroplasts

blocks.text: Photosynthesis needs energy. This section covers where the energy comes from and where the reaction happens.

items.meaning: A reaction that takes in energy from the surroundings.

items: Photosynthesis is an **endothermic** reaction.
The energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts by **light**.
Chlorophyll in the chloroplasts absorbs (traps) the light.
Algae also photosynthesise, because they have chlorophyll.
Photosynthesis is endothermic: it takes in energy.
The energy comes from light, absorbed by chlorophyll in the chloroplasts.

blocks.text: Photosynthesis is how energy from light enters living things. This section covers why plants and algae matter to every food chain.

items.meaning: An organism that makes its own food, here by photosynthesis.

items: Plants and algae are the main **producers** of food on Earth.
The glucose they make is used to build their biomass.
Other organisms get their food, and so their biomass, from plants and algae.
Photosynthesis also releases oxygen. When the number of algae in a river rises, the dissolved oxygen concentration rises.
Photosynthetic organisms are the main producers of food and biomass.
Algae photosynthesise too, so they add oxygen to water.

checks.q: Write the word equation for photosynthesis.
checks.a: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (light energy is needed).

checks.q: Describe how plants gain the energy for photosynthesis.
checks.a: They absorb light. The light is trapped by chlorophyll in the chloroplasts.

checks.q: The number of green algae in a river increases. Explain why the concentration of dissolved oxygen increases.
checks.a: The algae carry out photosynthesis, which produces oxygen.

worked_example.question:
Photosynthesis produces oxygen.

Complete the word equation for photosynthesis.

Choose answers from the box.

carbon dioxide   fat   glucose
nitrogen   protein   water

______ + ______ → ______ + oxygen
answer_points: water (left-hand side, 1 mark). The two reactants can be in either order.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each correct word. If you write words and formulae, the words are marked.

worked_example.question:
Some small plants are growing in the ground between the trees in a woodland. The leaves of the small plants are green.

Describe how these plants make glucose.
answer_points: They have chlorophyll / chloroplasts, which absorb (sun)light.
They carry out photosynthesis, in which water reacts with carbon dioxide (a word or symbol equation is accepted).
worked_example.tip: Any two of the four points earn the two marks: chlorophyll or chloroplasts, photosynthesis, absorbing light, water reacting with carbon dioxide.

worked_example.question: Describe the process of photosynthesis.
answer_points: Light is absorbed / collected by chlorophyll / chloroplasts. It takes place in the chloroplasts.
It is a two-stage process (a light-dependent and a light-independent stage).
Water is split into hydrogen and oxygen.
Carbon dioxide is combined with hydrogen to make glucose.
Any three of these points score. Identifying both the reactants and the products can earn 1 mark if the last two points are not awarded.
worked_example.tip: Name the reactants and products, say where it happens and what the light does.

blocks.text: Photosynthesis happens in two stages. This section gives a short description of each.

items: Light energy is absorbed by chlorophyll in the chloroplasts.
In the light-dependent stage, light energy splits water into hydrogen and oxygen. The oxygen is released.
Light energy is also used to make ATP.
In the light-independent stage, carbon dioxide is combined with hydrogen to make glucose.

worked_example.question: Describe the role of chlorophyll in photosynthesis.
answer_points: It transfers light energy into chemical energy.
The energy is used for the synthesis of glucose / carbohydrates.
worked_example.tip: Any two of the three points earn the two marks.

blocks.text: This section covers what chlorophyll does and how to investigate what photosynthesis needs.

items: Chlorophyll is a green pigment found in chloroplasts.
Chlorophyll transfers energy from light into chemical energy in the carbohydrates that are made.
Photosynthesis needs **chlorophyll**, **light** and **carbon dioxide**.
First destarch the plant by keeping it in the dark for 1 to 2 days.
Change only one factor and keep a control, so the result shows what that factor does.
Chlorophyll: use a variegated leaf. Only the green parts make starch.
Light: cover part of a leaf with foil. The covered part makes no starch.
Carbon dioxide: put the plant in sealed air with the carbon dioxide removed. The control has air with carbon dioxide.
Test a leaf for starch with iodine solution. Blue-black means starch is present, so photosynthesis happened.

worked_example.question:
Gas exchange in a flowering plant changes depending on conditions.

Plants carry out photosynthesis to produce ______. To enable this process to occur the leaf cells absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen.

At the same time the cells in the leaves are respiring. This means that they are using ______ and producing carbon dioxide. If the leaves are in bright sunlight, then the rate of photosynthesis will be ______ than the rate of respiration. If the leaves are in dim light, then the rate of respiration will be greater than the rate of photosynthesis and there will be a net production of ______.

In conditions when there is no net absorption or release of carbon dioxide the rate of photosynthesis and respiration are ______ and the plant is at its compensation point.

Complete the passage by writing a suitable word or words in each blank space.

blocks.text: This section covers gas exchange in leaves, which links photosynthesis to respiration.

items: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy, which is stored in glucose.
Photosynthesis takes in carbon dioxide and gives out oxygen. Respiration takes in oxygen and gives out carbon dioxide.
Both gases are waste products of one process and raw materials of the other.
Both gases move in and out of a leaf by diffusion through the stomata.
Respiration goes on day and night. Photosynthesis only goes on in the light.

items.meaning: The light intensity at which photosynthesis and respiration go at the same rate, so there is no net gas exchange.

items: In dim light, respiration is faster than photosynthesis, so the leaf gives out net **carbon dioxide**.
In bright light, photosynthesis is faster than respiration, so the leaf gives out net **oxygen**.
